audience.programmeDescription: Italian Studies at the University of Amsterdam combines learning Italian with the study of modern Italy’s history, society, literature and film. Students spend a semester at a partner university in Italy and finish with a thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers Renaissance Italian art, European politics, comparative literature and film. These courses do not form a sustained study of modern Italian society, history and culture. The UvA degree connects those subjects through Italian-language source work, translation and research.

componentNotes.ita-127111286y: The first year also includes a required Dutch writing diagnostic. Tutoring and study guidance continue each year. These requirements carry no credits.
componentNotes.ita-127121026y: Take Italian Language Proficiency and Culture 1 first.
componentNotes.ita-127121036y: Pass Italian Language Proficiency and Culture 1 and 2 first.
componentNotes.ita-127121046y: Pass Italian Language Proficiency and Culture 1 and 2 and take course 3 first.
componentNotes.ita-127121006y: Pass Italian Language Proficiency and Culture 1 and 2 and take courses 3 and 4 first.
componentNotes.ita-127211046y: Pass the first four Italian language proficiency courses first.
componentNotes.ita-127211056y: Pass the first four Italian language proficiency courses and take course 5 first.
componentNotes.ita-127221008y: Spend the second semester of year two at an approved partner university in Italy. Choose eligible subject courses in consultation with UvA.
componentNotes.ita-127221026y: Complete the programme’s Italian language proficiency sequence first.
componentNotes.ita-127211356y: Students in this degree must have taken the preceding Italian Studies courses.
componentNotes.ita-approved-free-profiling-space: Choose 30 EC of electives, a minor, an internship or eligible study abroad. Courses at another institution require approval. The usual first-year course limit is 12 EC, with specified exceptions up to 24 EC.
componentNotes.ita-127229012y: Pass all compulsory components before starting the thesis. The programme describes the thesis as written in Italian.

linkChecks: Official degree and curriculum pages and the dated programme, electives and individual-course records were retrieved.

mapping.search and title: The index uses the registered English title and the external-only heading also identifies the programme name Italian Studies. The official-source button uses the programme’s study page.
mapping.status and explanation: The exception type selects the no-match status and the reviewed audience explanation. It acknowledges substantive Renaissance Italian art and wider methods, and explains the missing modern-Italy focus, Italian sources and translation.
mapping.curriculum: The external-only table uses all 20 credited official component titles and the 14 stable notes. It distinguishes the compulsory 30 EC in Italy, 30 EC free choice, the thesis and noncredit formation. No UCR course description or optional independent research is selected for display.
